name: The demonic endowment
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16.4–20: hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance, leading to bondage; its bearers know neither engagement nor withdrawal, deny truth, foundation and a Lord, act from insatiable desire, boundless care and self-conceit, sacrifice in name only, hate the Lord in all bodies, fall into hell and are cast into demonic wombs.
antidotes: Abandoning desire, anger and greed (16.21–22); taking scripture as authority (16.24).

name: The three gates of hell: desire, anger, greed

names.name: The three gates of hell: desire, anger, greed

description: Desire, anger and greed are the threefold gate of hell, ruinous to the self, to be abandoned; one freed from these gates of darkness does what is good for the self and goes to the highest course (BhG 16.21–22).

name: Desire (kāma)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: insatiable desire is resorted to by the demonic (16.10); with anger and greed it is the threefold gate of hell (16.21); acting as desire prompts, casting aside scriptural injunction, one gains neither perfection, happiness nor the highest course (16.23); it is let go of in the discipline of 18.53.

name: Anger (krodha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: a mark of the demonic endowment (16.4) and a gate of hell (16.21); let go of in the discipline of 18.53.

name: Greed (lobha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16.21: the third gate of hell; the rājasic agent is greedy (18.27).

name: Hypocrisy of the unrealised (dambha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–17: hypocrisy/ostentation, first mark of the demonic endowment (16.4); the demonic act with it (16.10) and sacrifice with it (16.17); sacrifice for display (dambhārtham) is rājasic (17.12), austerity done with it is rājasic (17.18), and with egoism it drives unsanctioned terrible austerity (17.5).

name: Arrogance (darpa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā: arrogance, a mark of the demonic endowment (16.4), resorted to with ahaṅkāra, force, desire and anger by those who hate the Lord in all bodies (16.18); let go of, with these, in the discipline that makes one fit for becoming Brahman (18.53).

name: The sense of 'I' (ahaṃkāra)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: resorted to by the demonic (16.18) and by practitioners of unsanctioned austerity (17.5); action with it is rājasic (18.24); letting it go makes one fit for becoming Brahman (18.53); out of it Arjuna might not listen and perish, or resolve not to fight in vain (18.58–59); one without the sense 'I did it' does not slay though slaying (18.17).

name: Delusion (moha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: the demonic take up false notions out of delusion and are caught in its net (16.10, 16.16); abandoning obligatory action from delusion is tāmasic (18.7), as is action begun from it (18.25); Arjuna's refusal is from delusion (18.60); his confusion born of ignorance is destroyed at the end of the teaching (18.72–73).
antidotes: Hearing the teaching with one-pointed thought (18.72); the teacher's grace (18.73).

name: Ignorance veiling knowledge (ajñāna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: a mark of the demonic endowment (16.4); the demonic are deluded by ignorance (16.15); Arjuna's confusion is born of ignorance (18.72).

name: Lack of faith (aśraddhā)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 17.13, 17.28: sacrifice devoid of faith is tāmasic; whatever is offered, given, practised or done without faith is 'asat', of no account here or hereafter.

name: The sense of 'I am the doer' (kartṛtva-abhimāna)

names.name: The sense of 'I am the doer' (kartṛtva-abhimāna)

description: Bhagavad Gītā 18.16–17: since action has five causes, one of untrained understanding who sees the self alone as agent does not see; one without the sense 'I did it' does not slay though slaying and is not bound.

name: Cavilling (asūyā)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: the demonic are cavillers who hate the Lord in all bodies (16.18); the teaching is never to be told to one who cavils at the Lord (18.67); hearing without cavil brings the worlds of the meritorious (18.71).

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 18: sacrifice, giving and austerity are to be done giving up attachment (18.6, 18.9); sāttvic action is free of attachment (18.23) and the sāttvic agent is free of it (18.26).

name: Passion, attachment (rāga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 17–18: passion with desire drives unsanctioned austerity (17.5); the rājasic agent is passionate (18.27); sāttvic action is done without passion or aversion (18.23); passion and aversion are cast off in the discipline of 18.51.

name: Aversion (dveṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 18: the relinquisher does not hate disagreeable action (18.10); sāttvic action is done without passion or aversion (18.23); passion and aversion are cast off in the discipline of 18.51.

name: Conceit (māna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16.10, 16.17: conceit, with hypocrisy and arrogance, fills the demonic.

name: Possessiveness (parigraha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 18.53: possessions are let go of in the discipline that makes one fit for becoming Brahman.

name: Mine-ness and I-ness
description: Bhagavad Gītā: the demonic think 'this is mine, and this wealth too will be mine' (16.13); one without 'mine' (nirmama) is fit for becoming Brahman (18.53).

name: Laziness (ālasya)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 18.28, 18.39: the tāmasic agent is lazy; tāmasic happiness arises from sleep, sloth and heedlessness.

name: Heedlessness (pramāda)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 18.39: tāmasic happiness arises from sleep, sloth and heedlessness.

name: Grief (śoka)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: 'do not grieve' (16.5, 18.66); the rājasic agent is given to elation and grief (18.27); tāmasic steadiness does not let go of grief (18.35); the one become Brahman does not grieve (18.54).

name: Despondency (viṣāda)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 18.28, 18.35: the tāmasic agent is despondent; tāmasic steadiness does not let go of despondency.

name: Elation (harṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 18.27: the rājasic agent is given to elation and grief.

name: Fear (bhaya)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 18.35: tāmasic steadiness does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency and arrogance; the sāttvic understanding knows what is to be feared and not feared (18.30).

name: Bondage by the three guṇas
description: Bhagavad Gītā 18.40: there is no being on earth or in heaven among the gods free of the three guṇas born of prakṛti.
